p01.why: const auto& can bind a prvalue because the deduced type is const, giving const int&.

p02.why: The initializer names an overload set of two functions with no target type to choose one.

p03.why: decltype(auto) cannot have an initializer of the form = { ... }.

p04.why: An auto variable needs an initializer.

p05.why: decltype(auto) cannot be combined with const.

p06.why: A string literal gives a pointer to const of its character type.

p07.why: A name gives its declared type, a parenthesized lvalue gives int&, an xvalue gives int&&, and a prvalue gives int.

p08.why: left takes 3, 2, 1, then 0 ends the loop, so steps is 6 and main returns 0.

p09.why: A static const data member with an in-class initializer can use auto, and n is 1.

p10.why: An array of auto is not allowed.

p11.why: nullptr has type decltype(nullptr), which auto keeps.

p12.why: The braced range {1, 2.0} deduces initializer_list elements of two different types.

p13.why: Lvalues give T& keeping const, and prvalues and xvalues give T&&.

p14.why: The elements give int and double, which differ.

p15.why: auto cannot be combined with another type specifier.

p16.why: auto stands for int in each declarator, and later declarators can use a.

p17.why: Braces without = holding one expression give that expression's type.

p18.why: auto& keeps const and does not decay arrays, functions or the string literal array.

p19.why: inline static and static constexpr members can use auto; constexpr makes m const double.

p20.why: &once is a prvalue, so decltype(auto) gives the plain pointer type.

p21.why: The declared std::initializer_list lacks the pointer and count members and the constructor, so the compilers reject the deduction.

p22.why: The braced list must not be empty.

p23.why: auto& needs an lvalue unless the deduced type is const; 1 is a non-const prvalue.

p24.why: The initializer names an overload set that does not reduce to one function.

p25.why: decltype(auto) with braces holding more than one expression.

p26.why: The name of a function would deduce a function type.

p27.why: Each deduced type is int, which satisfies Int.

p28.why: Braces without = must hold exactly one expression.

p29.why: The variable occurs in its own initializer.

p30.why: A braced list inside parentheses is not permitted.

p31.why: decltype(auto) gives int[3], and an array cannot be initialized from another array.

p32.why: Braces without = holding one expression are allowed; {(i)} gives int&.

p33.why: With a properly shaped std::initializer_list declared, both give std::initializer_list<int>.

p34.why: Arrays, functions and string literals decay to pointers.

p35.why: Only the top-level const is dropped; the const below the pointer stays.

p36.why: auto stands for int in one declarator and double in the other.

p37.why: A static data member with auto needs an in-class initializer and inline, constexpr or const.

p39.why: const, volatile and * apply to the deduced type as written.

p40.why: once is a single function and each<long> names one specialization, so both decay to function pointers.

p42.why: References and top-level const and volatile are dropped, so all four are int.

p43.why: Placeholders work the same in if initializer statements, conditions and for initializer statements.

p44.why: Parentheses must hold exactly one expression.

p46.why: auto* needs an initializer of pointer type.

p47.why: A template name without arguments gives no single function to deduce from.

p48.why: An xvalue of const type is a valid initializer for auto&.

p49.why: The second declarator adds * and uses a, and auto is int in both.

p50.why: No std::initializer_list is declared before the deduction.

p52.why: A name gives its declared type, const int.

p53.why: With plain auto, the parenthesized expression gives its type without reference, so b is int.

p54.why: constexpr makes the variable const int.

p55.why: The deduced type double does not satisfy Int.
